situation.note: my 15 year old won't talk to me. door closed, headphones on. when I try he says I wouldn't understand. I worked so hard so he'd have it easier.

understanding.bridge: What you are living with is what the texts call expecting them to be different, and that is where this week begins.
understanding.week_thesis: Seven days from the ache of being shut out to seeing that his silence is his own, and your peace is still yours to keep.

week_beats.hook: You recognise the hurt of being dismissed by the child you gave everything for.
week_beats.diagnose: You see that the expectation of his understanding is what keeps the door closed.
week_beats.steady: You hold that your work was yours, and it was not wasted.
week_beats.act: You try letting go of his understanding, speaking your truth without demand, and taking one hour for yourself.
week_beats.story: A father who gave his son everything and was met with a closed door shows you that love does not end there.

understanding.core_struggle: A parent who worked hard to give their child a better life is now shut out by that same teenager who says they would not understand.
understanding.mirror: The door is closed, the headphones are on, and you are left with the work that was never enough.
understanding.insight: What they did hurts, and so does the picture you hold of how they were meant to be, which keeps breaking.

queries.hook: The ache of a child who once needed you and now says you wouldn't understand; the door closed, the headphones on, and the work you did that now feels unreceived.
queries.diagnose: Hurt grows from expecting others to act as we want; no one else can give us sorrow unless we hand them the reins of our peace.
queries.steady: Praise and blame, success and failure, ease and struggle, come and go; the work you did was yours, and it was not wasted.
queries.act: Let go of the need for his understanding, speak your truth to him gently and without demand, and find one hour that is yours alone.
queries.story: A father and son, a door closed, and the father who learned that love does not end when it is not received.

verse.speaker: Arjuna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna, who has collapsed in tears on the battlefield and refuses to fight.
verse.sanskrit: कार्पण्यदोषोपहतस्वभावःपृच्छामि त्वां धर्मसंमूढचेताः । यच्छ्रेयः स्यान्निश्चितं ब्रूहि तन्मेशिष्यस्तेऽहं शाधि मां त्वां प्रपन्नम् ॥
verse.line: I'm confused about what's right. Tell me plainly what's best; I'm ready to learn.
verse.translation: My nature is stricken by weakness and my mind is confused about what is right. I ask you: tell me for certain what is best for me. I am your student; I have come to you, teach me.
verse.why: Admitting you don't know and asking for help is where clarity begins.

prasang.title: Krishna and Arjuna on Arjuna's faint-heartedness
prasang.summary: Krishna challenges Arjuna's despair. Arjuna admits he is confused about what is right, cannot tell which choice is better, and asks Krishna to teach him.
prasang.lesson: Admitting you don't know and asking for help is where clarity begins.

verse.meaning: Arjuna stands on the field of battle, his body shaking, and he tells Krishna that his mind is caught in confusion. He asks Krishna to tell him exactly what is best. He admits he cannot see the right way forward and says he is ready to learn.
verse.for_you: You worked hard so your son would have it easier, and now he has shut the door. You feel hurt and dismissed. You are standing at your own field of battle, asking for plain direction.
verse.try_today: Notice one moment when you feel dismissed and do not try to fix it.
verse.scene_line: You stand on your own field, asking for plain direction after a door has closed.
asks: How do I ask for help without feeling weak?
Who can I ask for plain direction?

verse.speaker: Lakshman
verse.setting: Lakshman, keeping watch at night, to Guha who blames Kaikeyi for Ram sleeping on the ground.
verse.sanskrit: बोले लखन मधुर मृदु बानी। ग्यान बिराग भगति रस सानी॥ काहु न कोउ सुख दुख कर दाता। निज कृत करम भोग सबु भ्राता ॥
verse.line: No one else is the giver of your joy or sorrow. You live out the fruit of your own actions.
verse.translation: Then Lakshman spoke in a sweet, gentle voice, steeped in knowledge, detachment and devotion: "No one is the giver of another's joy or sorrow, brother. Everyone lives out the fruit of their own actions."

words.en: anyone) न (not) कोउ (anyone) सुख (pleasure) दुख (pain) कर (do) दाता (giver

verse.why: Before blaming someone for your pain, look at the whole chain of causes, including yourself.
verse.misuse: Not "you deserve your suffering"; it is about not handing your peace to others.

prasang.title: Lakshman and Guha by the sleeping Ram
prasang.summary: On the first night of exile, Guha the boatmen's chief sees Ram and Sita sleeping on grass and weeps with anger at Kaikeyi. Lakshman, keeping watch, tells him no one gives us joy or sorrow; we live out our own actions, so don't blame anyone needlessly.
prasang.lesson: Before blaming someone for your pain, look at the whole chain of causes, including yourself.

verse.meaning: Lakshman is awake on the first night of Ram's exile. Guha weeps and blames Kaikeyi for Ram sleeping on the ground. Lakshman answers that no one else gives you joy or sorrow. You live out the fruit of your own actions. He is asking Guha to look at the whole chain of causes before he points a finger.
verse.for_you: You are waiting for your son to say he understands the work you did for him. That expectation is the door he will not open. His silence is his own, and the ache you carry is the fruit of your own longing for a different answer.
verse.try_today: Notice your own hands when you reach for his doorknob.
verse.scene_line: You stand awake by the closed door, waiting for a fruit you planted yourself.
asks: What part of this ache is my own?
How do I stop giving him my peace?
What is the fruit of my own waiting?

verse.speaker: Bhartrihari
verse.sanskrit: निन्दन्तु नीतिनिपुणा यदि वा स्तुवन्तु लक्ष्मीः समाविशतु गच्छतु वा यथेष्टम् । अद्यैव वा मरणमस्तु युगान्तरे वा न्याय्यात्पथः प्रविचलन्ति पदं न धीराः ॥
verse.line: Let them praise or blame, let money come or go: the steady don't step off the right path.
verse.translation: Let the worldly-wise blame or praise; let fortune come or go as she pleases; let death come today or ages hence: the steadfast do not move a step from the path of what is right.
verse.why: Setbacks rarely last for those who keep going on the right path.

prasang.title: Nitishatakam: On steadfastness
prasang.summary: Steadfastness: the gods kept churning the ocean past jewels and poison until they found nectar; the steady do not leave the right path whatever people say. A struck ball bounces back and a cut tree grows again.
prasang.lesson: Setbacks rarely last for those who keep going on the right path.

verse.meaning: Bhartrihari is speaking to anyone who reads these verses. They are telling you to keep walking the path that is right for you. People will praise you or blame you. Money will come and go. Death can arrive today or in a hundred years. None of that should make you step off the path. The steady person does not move from the right way, no matter what happens around them.
verse.for_you: You worked hard to give your child a better life. That was your path. The praise or blame of others, the money, the silence from your son, none of it changes that. You did not waste your effort. The path you walked was yours.
verse.try_today: Notice one thing you did for your child today without needing thanks.

verse.speaker: Ribhu
verse.setting: Ribhu on inner stillness in an active life.
verse.sanskrit: बहिःकृत्रिमसंरंभो हृदि संरम्भवर्जितः । कर्ता बहिरकर्तान्तर्लोके विहर शुद्धधीः ॥
verse.line: Be busy on the outside and unhurried inside. Act fully, but don't let it agitate you.
verse.translation: Outwardly busy, inwardly free of agitation; a doer on the outside, a non-doer within: move through the world with a clear mind.
verse.why: Live fully in the world while staying unhurried inside.

prasang.title: How a free person lives
prasang.summary: Ribhu describes how a free person lives among others: letting go of what is lost, taking up what comes, doing the work at hand, speaking gently, busy outside and calm inside, and treating the whole world as family.
prasang.lesson: Live fully in the world while staying unhurried inside.

verse.meaning: Ribhu tells Nidagha what a free person looks like. They move through the world doing the work at hand, letting go of what is lost, taking up what comes. They speak gently and treat the whole world as family. Yet inside, they are unhurried and free of agitation. The verse proposes that you can act fully on the outside while keeping a clear, calm mind on the inside. The work is not the enemy. The agitation is.
verse.for_you: You worked hard so your son would have it easier. That effort was yours, and it was not wasted. Now the silence from behind his closed door is heavy. The work was yours. The peace is yours to keep.
verse.try_today: Notice one small thing you do at work and do it without hurry.
verse.scene_line: You are busy on the outside and unhurried inside while the silence waits.
asks: How do I hold my work without needing his approval?
Can I be calm while he stays shut away?
Is my peace only for when he finally talks?

verse.speaker: Hanuman
verse.setting: Hanuman has found Sita, terrified and alone; he works out how to speak without frightening her.
verse.sanskrit: अवश्यमेव वक्तव्यं मानुषं वाक्यमर्थवत्। मया सान्त्वयितुं शक्या नान्यथेयमनिन्दिता ॥
verse.line: To comfort someone, use their language, not the one that impresses.
verse.translation: I must speak to her in ordinary human words that carry meaning. There is no other way to comfort this blameless woman.
verse.why: Before a hard conversation, think about how the other person will hear you.

matched.label: My teenager won't listen to me

prasang.title: How Hanuman spoke to Sita
prasang.summary: Hanuman has found Sita but she is terrified. He thinks carefully: speak in ordinary language, not court Sanskrit; don't gamble on a fight; start by gently praising Ram so she can trust him. He sings Ram's story softly from the tree, and she hears hope for the first time: joy comes to the one who stays alive.
prasang.story_hook: He had found her at last, and now the problem was how to speak without making her scream.
prasang.lesson: Before a hard conversation, think about how the other person will hear you.

verse.meaning: Hanuman has found Sita in the garden, but she is terrified of this giant monkey. He knows he cannot speak to her in grand Sanskrit or courtly language, because she would only feel more fear. He decides to use ordinary human words, words that carry meaning and comfort. He thinks about how she will hear him before he speaks, and he starts by gently praising Rama so she can trust him. He shows that before any hard conversation, you could think about how the other person will hear you.
verse.for_you: You have worked hard for your son, and now he says you would not understand. He is shutting you out. Hanuman knew Sita needed ordinary words, not grand ones. You can speak your truth to your son without demanding he understand you right now.
verse.try_today: Speak one true thing to your son without asking for a reply.

verse.speaker: Bhartrihari
verse.setting: From the section on helping others: how the good behave.
verse.sanskrit: तृष्णां छिन्धि भज क्षमां जहि मदं पापे रतिं मा कृथाः सत्यं ब्रूह्यनुयाहि साधुपदवीं सेवस्व विद्वज्जनम् । मान्यान् मानय विद्विषोऽप्यनुनय प्रख्यापय प्रश्रयं कीर्तिं पालय दुःखिते कुरु दयामेतत् सतां चेष्टितम् ॥
verse.line: Cut craving, forgive, drop arrogance, speak truth, win over even enemies, be kind to those suffering.
verse.translation: Cut off craving, practise forbearance, give up arrogance, take no delight in wrong, speak the truth, follow the path of the good, serve the wise, honour those worthy of honour, win over even your enemies, show courtesy, guard your good name, be kind to those in pain: this is how the good behave.
verse.why: Success should make you bow lower; real ornaments are listening, giving and helping.
verse.misuse: Winning over an enemy is not the same as tolerating harm.

matched.label: I can't let go of resentment

prasang.title: Nitishatakam: On helping others
prasang.summary: Verses on generosity and friendship: trees bow with fruit, the hand shines by giving, a true friend keeps you from wrong and stays in trouble. Four kinds of people, from the selfless to those who harm for nothing.
prasang.lesson: Success should make you bow lower; real ornaments are listening, giving and helping.

verse.meaning: Bhartrihari speaks to the reader from a quiet place of observation, describing how the truly good live. They do not cling to results, do not let praise swell them, and do not let blame shrink them. They act fully in the world, but their inner ground stays steady. They serve the wise and honor the worthy. The verse says this is how the good behave: success should make them bow lower, and real ornaments are listening, giving, and helping.
verse.for_you: The door is closed and the headphones are on, and you are left with the ache of effort that feels unreceived. The verse asks you to drop the demand for his understanding and simply speak your truth without it. Your peace is not his to give.
verse.try_today: Take one hour today to be fully with yourself, not with him.
verse.scene_line: You are in your own home, the door is closed, and the good behave by standing steady.
asks: How do I speak my truth without demanding his understanding?
What does it mean to drop arrogance with someone I love?
How do I let his silence be his without making it mine?

story.title: Father and son go back to school
story.story_hook: When his son came home stumped, Uddalaka did something unusual for a famous teacher.
story.summary: A patron asks young Shvetaketu a question he cannot answer. He asks his father, who admits he does not know either and suggests they both go to the patron as students. Chitra welcomes Uddalaka for his humility.
story.lesson: A parent who says 'let's learn together' teaches more than any answer.

anchor.speaker: Shvetaketu and Uddalaka Aruni
anchor.setting: A patron asks Shvetaketu a question he cannot answer; he goes to his father.
anchor.sanskrit: स होवाच नाहमेतद्वेद हन्ताचार्यं प्रच्छानीति स ह पितरमासाद्य पप्रच्छेतीति स होवाचाहमप्येतन्न वेद सदस्येव वयं स्वाध्यायमधीत्य हरामहे यन्नः परे ददत्येह्युभौ गमिष्याव इति ॥
anchor.line: 'I don't know either,' the father told his son. 'Let's both go and learn, as students.'
anchor.translation: He said, 'I do not know this. Let me ask my teacher.' He went to his father and asked. The father said, 'I too do not know it. We have studied the Veda and take what others give us. Come, let us both go.'
anchor.why: A parent who says 'let's learn together' teaches more than any answer.
